questions.q: What is your first High Volume Edge buy?
questions.story: A trial result hits at 7 a.m. The stock trades far higher pre-market on huge volume and holds all day.
choices: Day 2, a reclaim of the HVC
Pre-market, before it runs
The open, over the first high
The record day's close
questions.answer: Day 2, a reclaim of the HVC
questions.why: Day 2, a reclaim of the HVC. No buys outside regular trading hours, so the pre-market spike is not a buy. The taught trigger is day 2, the one session after the record day: it dips under the record day's close and trades back over it. Buying the open over the first high is the Episodic Pivot's trade on the gap day, a different setup. The news sets the level. Day 2 sets the trade.
questions.lesson_line: The news sets the level. Day 2 sets the trade.

wrong.The open, over the first high: That is the Episodic Pivot's entry on the gap day. Ours waits for day 2.
wrong.The record day's close: The close is the level, not the buy.

questions.simple: Your first buy is on day 2, when price dips under the HVC and reclaims it. We never buy pre-market.

deeper.trap: The trap is that the news arrives before the open. A pre-market spike is not a regular-hours buy, and the record day's close is the level, not the entry. Bonde buys the event day pre-market, and Kullamagi waits for the opening-range high on the gap day. We wait for day 2, then buy the trade back over the HVC.

reasons: +2 rests on the owner's rulebook (E58) and the held D-005 (whether a close entry is taught)
+1 fixed before (the question was reworded)

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the last bar is the record day. Plan the day-2 trade or pass?
choices: Plan day 2; a fresh start
Pass; a climax after a run
Pass; it is under the 200-day
Buy the close; it is a record
questions.why: Plan day 2. This is a neglected stock with a fresh story. It had a flat line for six months, 16% under its 200-day, then a 126% gap on 18x volume, an all-time record. No run came before it, so it is a start and not a climax. Sitting under the 200-day before the record day does not rule it out, because the rule reads the trade at entry. The HVC was never traded again, and the stock added 68% by day 59.
questions.lesson_line: A quiet stock, a new story, record volume: mark the close and plan day 2.

wrong.Pass; a climax after a run: There was no run before it. Six flat months, then the record day.
wrong.Pass; it is under the 200-day: The rule reads the trade at entry, not the stock before the record day.
wrong.Buy the close; it is a record: The taught trigger is day 2, not the record day's close. The close is the level, not the buy.

questions.simple: Plan day 2. A quiet stock, a fresh story, record volume and no run before it make a start, not a climax.

deeper.trap: Look left first. The 200-day choice tempts because the stock sat under the line before the event. But the rule reads the trade at entry, not the stock before the record day. Then test for a run. This stock was flat for six months, so the climax test of a 60% run in 60 sessions did not apply.

reasons: rests on dossier reads of the example, not on the picture

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the last bar is a record-volume day. Plan the day-2 trade or pass?
choices: Pass; a climax after a run
Plan day 2; it is record volume
Plan day 2; it doubled in price
Pass; it is too late to chase
questions.answer: Pass; a climax after a run
questions.why: Pass. The close before the record day was 72.5% over the lowest low of the prior 60 sessions. The card rules out a run of 60% or more, so this is a climax, not a start. The day was +102.5% on 18.2x volume, 3.2x the old record, and that size does not fix it. Taken anyway, day 2 opened 3% under the HVC, triggered, and the trade was stopped at 0.0R. The stock topped within two months.
questions.lesson_line: Look left before you mark the level. A record after a big run is a climax.

wrong.Plan day 2; it is record volume: Record volume after a 60% run in 60 sessions is a climax, not our start.
wrong.Plan day 2; it doubled in price: The size of the day does not fix the run before it.
wrong.Pass; it is too late to chase: Day 2 is not a chase: the HVE waits for a dip under the HVC and a reclaim. The pass is for the long run before it.

questions.simple: Pass. The stock had already run up a lot, so a record day there is a climax and not a start.

deeper.trap: The run is measured from the lowest low of the prior 60 sessions to the close before the record day. A big, real record day does not rescue it. This one was 3.2x the old record and still a climax. Look left before you mark the level.

reasons: rests on dossier reads of the example, not on the picture

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A record day closes at 45.00. Day 2 opens 44.20, trades between 43.60 and 44.70, and closes 44.00. You are flat.
choices: Nothing; no trigger, no trade
Buy at the close, 44.00 a share
Wait, then buy day 3 at the open
Erase the level; it failed
questions.why: Nothing. Day 2 never trades back over the HVC, so there is no trigger and no trade. The level stays on the chart, because the chart may give a later entry there. A close under the HVC is not an invalidation. No setup, no trade. Cash is a position.
questions.lesson_line: No setup, no trade. Keep the line and wait.

wrong.Buy at the close, 44.00 a share: No trigger came. The buy is a trade back over the HVC.
wrong.Erase the level; it failed: Keep it. A close under the HVC is not an invalidation, and later setups form at the level.
wrong.Wait, then buy day 3 at the open: The taught trigger is day 2, not a later day. A later entry needs one of our own setups at the level, not a buy at the open.

questions.simple: Do nothing. Day 2 never traded back over 45.00, so there was no trigger, and the level stays on the chart.

deeper.trap: Do not turn a no-trigger day into a trade by bending the rule. The low was 43.60 and the high 44.70, so the day never traded back over 45.00. The level can still give a later entry on one of our own setups, each with its own trigger and stop.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (D44, no setup no trade)
